The eternal struggle with Microsoft Word's styles!

To achieve the desired behavior where your "Titre2" style is linked to your "Titre1" style and increments correctly, you can follow these steps:

1. Open the Styles pane in Microsoft Word by going to the Home tab > Styles group > Style Pane button (or press F11).
2. Select the "Titre1" style, then click on the "Modify" button at the bottom of the Styles pane.
3. In the Modify Style dialog box, select the "Format" button and choose "Paragraph".
4. In the Paragraph dialog box, go to the "Tabs" tab (or "Indents and Spacing" in newer versions of Word).
5. Click on the "Reset" button to clear any existing tabs.
6. Set up a new tab by clicking on the "New Tab" button. Name this tab something like "Titre2".
7. In the "Before" text box, enter a space (or a number of spaces) that corresponds to the indentation you want for your second-level titles.
8. Click OK to close the Paragraph dialog box and return to the Styles pane.
9. Repeat steps 2-6 for the "Titre2" style, but this time set up the tab with the same settings as step 7.

Now, when you apply the "Titre1" style to a paragraph and then apply the "Titre2" style to a sub-paragraph (by pressing Enter or using the "Apply Styles" button), Microsoft Word will automatically indent the sub-paragraph according to the settings you defined in steps 6 and 7.

As for the incrementing part, this should happen naturally since you're using the same style ("Titre1") as the parent paragraph. When you apply the "Titre2" style to a new sub-paragraph, Word will automatically reset the level counter, so you'll get "1.1", then "2.1", and so on.

I hope this helps!
